Reply. As mentioned on p. 19 of the Draft, the core hole will be cased in the upper 75-m, preventing seepage into the surrounding permeable firn. Permeability below the firn is negligible because of the high density of ice. The drilling fluid will not enter the sea under the ice shelf because seawater will rise in the bottom of the hole as soon as the ice shelf is penetrated by drilling. Diesel fuel is less dense and will remain on top of the seawater. When operations in the hole are completed, the diesel fuel will be recovered from the hole as it is displaced by the water.
Paragraph 3 - Sanitary wastes.
Reply. Incinerator toilets were considered but not found necessary as standard Antarctica disposal as described under Liquid-waste Disposal p. 26 is a reasonable method.
Paragragh 4 - Use of explosives to open the last few meters of ice in the drill hole.
Reply. There will be no noise effects on personnel at the surface because the shot will occur at the bottom of the hole, about 450 meters below the surface. A minor shock wave might extend to the surface.
As far as damage to the local biota (if any exist) is concerned, this will also be very minimal, as the shot will occur in the drill hole, blowing the remaining ice out of the bottom. Water will provide a damping effect, however, so ice fragments will not carry far, nor will the resulting shock waves. The present plans do not require the use of any change to open the bottom of the hole. This is now considered a contingency which will be used only as a last resort.
